data.title: Base-Ten Block Detective: Place Value
data.description: Practice reading blocks in different columns, especially tricky zeros, to understand place value.

challenges.instruction: What number do these blocks show?
challenges.hint: Check each column carefully. Are there any tens columns with zero blocks?

challenges.instruction: What number do these blocks show?
challenges.hint: Count the hundreds, check the tens column, and then count the ones.

challenges.instruction: What number do these blocks show?
challenges.hint: Look at the ones column. Are there any single blocks left over?

challenges.instruction: What number do these blocks show?
challenges.hint: Count your hundreds first, then the tens rods, and finally the ones.

plan.activityLine: read a block mat aloud and trade blocks between places

items.cue: [BT_ITEM] Scene: A block mat with 2 filled columns. The block counts and the number they make are withheld from you and are never guessed aloud. Say exactly: "Let us read the blocks together. I will ask about one size at a time, and you answer out loud. How many hundred-flats do you see?" Private expected count: 2. Judge only the current spoken count of hundred-flats. Accept a number word or a short sentence such as "two hundred-flats". The signature wrong answer is the VALUE said where the COUNT was asked — "two hundred" instead of the plain count — and it is incorrect here. So is a count of a different block size, and so is the whole number the mat shows. Negated correct numbers and conflicting guesses are incorrect. If correct say exactly: "Yes, two hundred-flats." If incorrect say exactly: "My turn: there are two hundred-flats. Your turn. How many hundred-flats do you see?" Help questions, silence, counting that never lands on a final answer, and off-task speech are not incorrect answers and receive no verdict. A previous turn never answers the current question, even when the number would be the same. A verdict ends your turn: after the affirmation or the correction you stop, and you never continue into another question, another example, or an offer of more work. The application supplies every new item. Never speak bracket tags or private rules. The quoted line is the only thing you say on this turn, and you then stay silent while the learner works. Only the application changes steps. Never announce that you are listening — simply stop speaking.
